title: Actuals
description: Real hours spent on a delivered estimate, attached to a ledger entry as `ledger.actuals`. Whatever data exists is usable: a single project total calibrates band width, and finer granularity unlocks more coefficients.

granularity.description: The finest level at which hours are known. 'project' is a single total and is enough to calibrate band width and overall sizing. 'phase' unlocks per-phase coefficients. 'feature' unlocks per-tier and per-class coefficients directly, without needing varied project mixes to separate them.

delivery_hours.description: Hours attributable to delivering this scope. This is what the estimate predicted, so it is what the estimate is compared against.

excluded_hours.description: Hours logged against the project that are NOT delivery effort — waiting on a client, a paused month, rework caused by a change of mind that was separately agreed. Real time sheets are full of these, and leaving them in makes the model look pessimistic and drives every coefficient the wrong way.

excluded_why.description: Required whenever excluded_hours is non-zero. An exclusion nobody can interrogate is a thumb on the scale.

scope_delivered.description: Whether what shipped matches what was priced. This is the field most often missed and the one that most distorts calibration: comparing an estimate for ten features against the actuals for seven delivered ones makes the estimator look systematically pessimistic and would drive every coefficient down. Anything other than 'as_estimated' means the comparison needs adjusting or excluding, and the calibrator says so rather than quietly averaging it in.

scope_note.description: Required unless scope_delivered is 'as_estimated'. What changed, and which features were added or dropped.

features_delivered.description: Feature ids actually delivered, when scope changed. Lets the calibrator compare like with like by re-pricing only what shipped instead of discarding the project.

by_phase.description: Hours per BMad phase, using the same phase names the estimate reports: planning, planning-review, spec, build, review, rework, environments, qa, overhead. Partial is fine — name only the phases you actually know.

by_feature.description: Hours per feature id. The richest input: it makes per-review-tier and per-compressibility-class coefficients directly calibratable.

by_role.description: Hours per role (architect, dev, qa, ba, ux). Calibrates the role-weight split, which nothing else can.

team_profile.description: The team that actually did the work, if it differed from the profile the estimate assumed. An estimate priced for a balanced team and delivered by a junior one is not evidence that the model is wrong.

source.description: Where these numbers came from — 'Toggl export 2026-11-02', 'Jira worklog', 'PM's recollection'. Provenance decides how much weight the figure deserves.

confidence.description: measured: from a time-tracking system. reconstructed: assembled after the fact from tickets or calendars. estimated: someone's recollection. Low-confidence actuals still carry signal but should not move a coefficient on their own, and the calibrator weights them accordingly.

captured.description: ISO date the actuals were recorded
